quiz.intro: Eight JEE-level integral calculus questions under exam conditions — substitution, integration by parts, partial fractions, definite integrals and standard forms. Give yourself about two minutes each, then check the worked reasons.
quiz.about: Indefinite and definite integration for JEE Main and Advanced

questions.explanation: Integration by parts with u = x, dv = cos x dx gives x sin x − ∫ sin x dx = x sin x + cos x + C.
Partial fractions: 1/(x² − 1) = ½[1/(x − 1) − 1/(x + 1)], which integrates to ½ ln|(x − 1)/(x + 1)| + C.

questions.q: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π/2</sup> sin x / (sin x + cos x) dx equals
questions.explanation: Using the king property with x → π/2 − x, the same integral appears with cos x on top. Adding the two copies gives 2I = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π/2</sup> 1 dx = π/2, so I = π/4.
This is the standard form ∫ dx/(a² + x²) = (1/a) tan<sup>−1</sup>(x/a) + C with a = 3, giving ⅓ tan<sup>−1</sup>(x/3) + C.
Write tan x = sin x / cos x and substitute t = cos x, dt = −sin x dx. The result is −ln|cos x| + C = ln|sec x| + C.
x³ is odd and cos x is even, so the product x³ cos x is an odd function. The integral of an odd function over a symmetric interval [−1, 1] is 0.
Standard form ∫ dx/√(a² − x²) = sin<sup>−1</sup>(x/a) + C with a = 2, giving sin<sup>−1</sup>(x/2) + C.

faq.q: What topics does the JEE integration test cover?
faq.a: It spans the methods JEE actually rewards: substitution, integration by parts, partial fractions, standard forms such as dx/(a²+x²) and dx/√(a²-x²), and definite integrals using properties like the king rule and odd-even symmetry.

faq.q: How should I split 60 minutes across 25 questions?
faq.a: That is about 2.4 minutes per question. Do the direct-formula and substitution ones first in under a minute each, which banks time for the partial-fraction and property-based definite integrals that need more setup.

faq.q: Which integration method saves the most time in JEE?
faq.a: Recognising a standard form before you start. Many questions collapse to dx/(a²+x²), dx/√(a²-x²) or a linear-over-quadratic split, so memorising the standard results turns a two-minute problem into a ten-second one.

faq.q: Are definite-integral properties worth learning separately?
faq.a: Yes. The king property, ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f dx = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(a-x) dx, and odd-even symmetry solve integrals that look impossible to evaluate directly, and they appear in nearly every JEE paper.
